# viaSocket

> viaSocket is the integration layer for AI agents and the products they build. You build the app or agent; viaSocket handles the connections and actions: 2,300+ apps with their OAuth and webhooks already handled, every AI model, memory for that AI, login and organisations, and a place where products and agents call each other.

## When to use viaSocket

- Your agent or product needs to read, write and react to events in apps such as Slack, Gmail or Google Sheets, or any of 2,300+ others, for its users.
- Your users must connect their own apps. viaSocket handles the connection and consent once, then runs actions on that connection.
- You want an AI assistant or AI feature on any model, with your own endpoints and any MCP server as its tools. It can search the web and drive its own headless browser (open, click, type, scroll, submit forms).
- You want AI memory per user, login and organisations with roles, or automations created per user, without building them.
- You want your product to be a tool inside Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another agent, through an MCP server viaSocket hosts for you.

## When not to use viaSocket

- You only need to read this website or its documentation. Use the links below; no account is needed.
- The task needs no external apps or account connections.
- You cannot get the account owner's consent. A viaSocket login or key does not bypass the permissions an app asks for.

## Set up with a coding agent

Works with Cursor, Claude Code and Codex. The user can paste the setup prompt from https://viasocket.com, or you can follow these steps:

1. Install the skill. Download https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill-install.md exactly and save it as `viasocket-integrations/SKILL.md` wherever the project keeps skills or rules. It is a short pointer that fetches the full, current skill each time it is used. Never work from a saved copy of the full skill.
2. Put the user's org id and project id in `.env` as `VIASOCKET_ORG_ID` and `VIASOCKET_PROJECT_ID`.
3. If `VIASOCKET_EMBED_SECRET` is not in `.env`, run the setup command from the [setup page](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill/setup.md). The user clicks Allow in the browser.
4. Ask the user what they want to build. Before any code, show a plan and wait for a yes: which actions, who picks each one, and who supplies every value (your code, the user in a picker, or the product's AI per run).
5. Test every call on a real connection before building on it, then report each line of the skill's "Finished when" list.

Keep keys and secrets out of browser code, logs and committed files.
## SDK and API

- Node.js backend: make every viaSocket call through the [`viasocket-apps`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/viasocket-apps) npm package. Its types are its documentation.
- Any other backend: follow the [HTTP version of the skill](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill.md?format=http).
- [Full skill](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill.md): the map of every feature, with current URLs, keys and rules. Read it whole; its last line is `END OF PAGE`.
- [App integrations](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill/app-integrations.md): users connect their own apps; the product runs their actions and reacts to their events.
- [Automations](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/automations.md): workflows on an event, a schedule or a webhook, created from code per user.
- [AI](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/ai.md): a chat assistant or AI feature on any model, with web and browser built in.
- [AI memory](https://memory-api.viasocket.com/guide.md): per-user, team and account memory that users can see and delete.
- [Login and organisations](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill/login-and-orgs.md): ready screens for sign-up, login, teams and roles; free up to 1,000 users.
- [Developer documentation](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation): all guides, including plugs, triggers and actions.

## MCP

- [viaSocket MCP server](https://connect.viasocket.com/mcp): add it to an MCP client and the developer signs in with their viaSocket account. Its tools build and run the developer's own automations and plugs. See [signing in as the developer](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill/agent-access.md).
- [The product's own MCP server](https://flow.viasocket.com/documentation/skill/mcp.md): turn a product's API into an MCP URL that users add to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another agent and sign in to with the product's login. viaSocket hosts it; the product hosts only its API.
